ABOUT & EDUCATION

I want to understand
what I’m building.

I’m a mechanical engineering student working on robotics, from actuator design to control software.

Jiale Jiang · Southern California

From an equation
to a working part.

An equation makes more sense to me when I can connect it to something I can build and measure. I’ve followed that interest from a ducted ROV thruster to printed actuators and a twelve-joint quadruped.

On the robot, a change in one subsystem often affects another. I’ve learned to check assumptions, write down what happened in a test, and explain the interfaces to the people working with me.

I’m studying mechanical engineering at Mount San Antonio College while continuing the robotics work with teammates and studying controls on my own.

TOOLS I USE IN MY PROJECTS

Tools from CAD to control.

Mechanical design

SolidWorks, parametric CAD, FDM prototyping, assembly design, engineering drawings, structural and flow analysis.

Electronics & embedded

KiCad, STM32 development, magnetic encoder circuits, PCB assembly and rework, CAN communication, bench diagnostics.

Software & modeling

Python, C++, Eigen, Linux / SocketCAN, MATLAB, MuJoCo, analytical kinematics, numerical validation, reinforcement learning experiments.

Help teammates take ownership.

I’ve taught teammates soldering and actuator assembly and helped them work through CAN setup and testing. For the IMU subsystem, I worked through the reasoning with teammates while they took responsibility for the implementation.
